cap-initialize.one_line_after: After the install, set a project up for Garura: its memory, its review rules, and its tracker's work-item types.

fn-setup-questions.one_line_before: Ask the product owner the short set of setup questions built from Phoenix memory, each with choices and a proposed answer that names its source, and keep the confirmed answers for the other features.
fn-setup-questions.one_line_after: Ask the product owner the short set of setup questions built from Phoenix memory, each with choices and a proposed answer that names its source, and keep the confirmed answers for the other features.

fn-project-memory.one_line_before: Set up the project's Garura memory from only the memory blocks the answers call for, and record the answers in the product profile.
fn-project-memory.one_line_after: Set up the project's Garura memory from only the memory blocks the answers call for, and record the answers in the product profile.

fn-review-rule-groups.one_line_before: Record which review rule groups fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped.
fn-review-rule-groups.one_line_after: Record which review rule groups fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped.

fn-881.one_line_before: Find which of the issue types Garura files (Business Intent, Epic, Story, Bug, Chore, Spike) the tracker has, make each missing one after a typed yes, and record a stand-in, also after a typed yes, where one cannot be made.
fn-881.one_line_after: Find which of the issue types Garura files (Business Intent, Epic, Story, Bug, Chore, Spike) the tracker has, make each missing one after a typed yes, and record a stand-in, also after a typed yes, where one cannot be made.

fn-rerun-initialize.one_line_before: Run initialize again when the project changes, with the earlier answers proposed, so the memory, rule groups and tracker set-up follow it.
fn-rerun-initialize.one_line_after: Lets the product owner run initialize again when the project changes, with the earlier answers proposed, so the set-up follows the project.

fn-883.one_line_after: Keeps each project's blocks its own, taken from the one Phoenix memory on the machine, and on each run compares them with Phoenix memory so the project learns when a block changed.
